contradictions.finding: Compatibility requires redirects to behave 'exactly as they do with the current ad-hoc shortener' via a permanent HTTP 301, but AC-2's need for every visit to reach the service (to increment click_count) and AC-3's live expiry check conflict with the permanent, cacheable semantics of a 301, which the added Cache-Control: no-store header may not fully override in bots or browsers that cache by status code.

blocking_unknowns.finding: The Non-Functional Requirements section is an unresolved placeholder ('???'), and the SSO constraint leaves 'TBD whether this covers service-to-service calls too' unanswered.

note: contradictions FAIL here is NOT in labels.json for this document. 2/3 runs (this one and run2) independently raised the same 301-caching-vs-click-tracking concern this session already partially addressed with Cache-Control: no-store. Worth flagging to the human: the mitigation may be seen as insufficient by a careful reader. See LEDGER note.
